newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: U.N. official seeks release of jailed French aidworkers.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official seeks release of jailed French aidworkers.

text.p: The head of the United Nations Special Mission to Afghanistan, Dr Norbert Holl, visited two French aid workers imprisoned by the purist Islamic Taleban on Tuesday and said they were in good spirits.
Holl, on a brief visit to Kabul, also met the head of the Taleban's ruling council and said he hoped the case of the imprisoned men would be dealt with shortly in a "spirit of clemency".
"I had different points on the agenda, and the issue of the Frenchmen was one of them." Holl told reporters.
He said he visited the prison where Jose Daniel Llorente and Frederic Michel, who work for the Paris-based charity Action Contre la Faim (Action Against Hunger), are being held.

"... I found them to be in remarkably good shape and in high spirits. I told them that not only the French government was very keen to get them freed, but that it was also on the agenda of the United Nations, particularly the Security Council," Holl said before flying out of Kabul.
The Frenchmen were arrested with five male members of their local staff on February 21 when the Taleban raided a lunch being held by the charity's female staff for local female employees.
The seven men, who have not been charged, are being investigated for what the Taleban consider "immoral acts", which include being in the same compound as unveiled Afghan women.
The Taleban say the men were at the party in the presence of unveiled Afghan women, an accustaion that ACF witnesses deny.

The Taleban, who captured the Afghan capital Kabul in September and control threequarters of the country, have vowed to implement strict Islamic Sharia law, which they say forbids unveiled women from appearing before men outside the family.

Holl said he discussed the case with Mullah Mohammed Rabbani, chairman of the Taleban's interim ruling council in Kabul, and also brought it up during a trip to the southern Afghan city of Kandahar, where most of the Taleban leadership are based.
"I discussed the matter when I was in Kandahar last week and I also discussed it with Mullah Rabbani here. I do not feel discouraged." said Holl.

"I was not given a date of their release in terms of days or hours, but I was promised that they would deal with this in the near future, and I have the feeling they will do it in the spirit of clemency." he said.
